text: It is an appointment. <break time="0.8s" /> That we made twenty years ago. <break time="0.8s" /> The man went on. <break time="0.8s" /> It sounds a little funny to you. <break time="0.8s" /> I am sure so I will explain. <break time="0.8s" /> There used to be a restaurant. <break time="0.8s" /> Where this store stands. <break time="0.8s" /> Big Joe Bradys restaurant. <break time="0.8s" /> It was here until five years ago. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the policeman. <break time="0.8s" /> Then it was torn down. <break time="0.8s" /> The man in the doorway. <break time="0.8s" /> Struck a match. <break time="0.8s" /> And lit his cigar. <break time="0.8s" /> The light showed. <break time="0.8s" /> A pale face. <break time="0.8s" /> With a square jaw and sharp eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> There was also. <break time="0.8s" /> A little white scar. <break time="0.8s" /> Near his right eyebrow. <break time="0.8s" /> His scarfpin was a large diamond. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was set in a strange way. <break time="0.8s" /> Twenty years ago tonight. <break time="0.8s" /> I ate dinner here. <break time="0.8s" /> With Jimmy Wells. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was my best friend. <break time="0.8s" /> We grew up here in New York. <break time="0.8s" /> Like two brothers. <break time="0.8s" /> I was eighteen. <break time="0.8s" /> And Jimmy was twenty. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning. <break time="0.8s" /> I was leaving for the West. <break time="0.8s" /> But Jimmy would never leave New York. <break time="0.8s" /> We agreed to meet here again. <break time="0.8s" /> In exactly twenty years. <break time="0.8s" /> No matter what happened.
